dimensions.note: No credentials: kind and kubectl use the caller's own docker and kubeconfig.
ensure, get and delete log what they do (create, exists, apply each manifest, delete, already gone) with structured placeholders.
A failing kind or kubectl throws with its argv and stderr; an existing cluster whose API server does not answer throws with how to restart its container, before anything is written.

A fake kind/kubectl covers create-when-missing, leave-when-present, unreachable API server (no write), get without creating, delete when already gone, and the argv/stderr error; ensure, a second ensure, delete and a second delete were also run live against a real kind cluster.
ensure creates only when kind get clusters does not list the cluster and re-applies the manifests (kubectl apply is idempotent); delete succeeds when the cluster is already gone.
No HTTP calls; kind and kubectl output is read as text (cluster names, the server URL).
Subprocess output is read to the end; the cluster created is recorded by name and context so delete can remove it.
README uses placeholders; no addresses or identifiers.
The cluster spec is lifetime infinite with garbageCollection 10.
ensure (create), get (read), delete; a kind cluster has no update beyond re-applying manifests, which ensure does.
The mutating methods act on a local kind cluster the definition names.
Nothing is read back from stored state.
Initial version of @dataverket/kind/cluster (ported from Salmon's @eskpil/kind-cluster). 2026.10.27.1 relicenses the extension to AGPL-3.0-only (LICENSE.md, manifest license, README); no code change.
